title: Service Costing
outcomes: Choose suitable cost units for services.
Compute transport costs using absolute and commercial tonne-km.
Cost and price hotel, hospital and other services.

meta.exam_tip: Compute the service units (room-days, tonne-km) first; every rupee answer divides by them.

concepts.title: Features of service costing and cost units
body: Service costing (operating costing) finds the cost of services such as transport, power, hotels, hospitals, education, IT and toll roads. Services cannot be stored, are largely fixed-cost businesses, and need cost units that capture the work done.
Composite cost units combine two measures: passenger-km, tonne-km, room-day, patient-day, kilowatt-hour, student-hour, vehicle-km.
Costs are classified as fixed (standing) charges, semi-variable (maintenance) charges and variable (running) charges, and collected on a log sheet or service cost sheet.
concepts.analogy: A good cost unit captures both "how much" and "how far" or "how long".
concepts.work: A bus company uses passenger-km because both passengers carried and distance matter.

concepts.title: Transport costing
body: Absolute tonne-km (or passenger-km) = sum of (load × distance) for each leg.
Commercial tonne-km = average load × total distance, where average load is the simple average of loads on the legs.

Standing charges: garage rent, insurance, road tax, driver's salary, depreciation (if time-based); running charges: fuel, oil, tyres, depreciation (if usage-based); maintenance: repairs, servicing. Fare or freight = cost per unit plus profit margin.
concepts.analogy: Absolute tonne-km tracks each leg exactly; commercial tonne-km uses the average.
concepts.work: A bus with 40 passengers for 50 km does 2,000 passenger-km.

concepts.title: Hotels, hospitals and other services
body: Hotels: room-day or bed-night; occupancy rate is crucial, and costs such as laundry, food and housekeeping are separated by department.
Hospitals: patient-day or bed-day for wards; per test for labs; per procedure for operation theatres. Idle capacity costs must be watched.

Other services: power (kWh), education (student-year), IT and ITeS (per user or per transaction), toll roads (per vehicle crossing; build-operate-transfer model needs recovery of investment over the concession period).
concepts.analogy: Pricing a service is recovering largely fixed costs over expected usage.
concepts.work: A 100-bed hospital at 75% occupancy over 365 days provides 27,375 patient-days.

illustrations.title: Measuring a truck's work
illustrations.q: A truck carries 8 tonnes from Nashik to Pune (100 km) and unloads it all; it then carries 5 tonnes from Pune to Satara (60 km). Trip costs: fuel ₹4,800, driver ₹3,000, other ₹1,500. Compute absolute and commercial tonne-km and cost per absolute tonne-km.

illustrations.title: Pricing a hotel room
illustrations.q: Lakeview Hotel has 50 rooms, open 360 days a year, with expected occupancy of 80%. Total annual cost is ₹1,15,20,000. Compute cost per room-day and the room rent to earn 20% on cost.

checks.label: Rent per room-day for 20% profit on cost

jobs.title: Freight rate setting
jobs.situation: A fleet owner wants a freight rate per tonne-km for a new route.
steps: Estimate distance and loads per leg.
Classify costs as standing, running and maintenance.
Add margin and compare with market rates.
jobs.takeaway: Empty return trips raise cost per tonne-km sharply.

mcqs.q: The cost unit for a hospital ward is usually:
mcqs.explain: Patient-day (or bed-day) captures patients and time. In practice: labs use cost per test.
mcqs.topic: Features of service costing and cost units

mcqs.q: A bus carries 30 passengers for 40 km and 20 passengers for 60 km. Passenger-km:
mcqs.explain: 30 × 40 + 20 × 60 = 1,200 + 1,200 = 2,400. In practice: use for fare per passenger-km.

options: Sum of load × distance per leg
mcqs.explain: The average of loads on each leg multiplied by total distance. In practice: absolute tonne-km is leg-wise.

mcqs.q: Which is a standing charge in transport costing?
mcqs.explain: Insurance is fixed regardless of distance. The others vary with running. In practice: driver salary is usually standing.

mcqs.q: Hotel with 40 rooms, 300 days, 75% occupancy. Room-days:
mcqs.explain: 40 × 300 × 75% = 9,000. In practice: divide total cost by this.
Operating costing applies to services. In practice: power and transport are common examples.
mcqs.topic: Features of service costing and cost units

mcqs.q: Cost per room-day ₹1,000; required profit 25% on rent. Rent:
mcqs.explain: 1,000 ÷ 0.75 = ₹1,333. In practice: 25% on cost would give ₹1,250.

mcqs.q: Toll road costing under BOT recovers:
options: Construction and operating costs over the concession period
mcqs.explain: Build-operate-transfer projects price tolls to recover investment and running costs before handover. In practice: traffic forecasts drive the toll.

summary: Composite units: tonne-km, passenger-km, room-day, patient-day, kWh.
Absolute t-km = Σ load × distance; commercial = average load × total distance.
Hotels and hospitals: occupancy drives unit cost.
remember: Profit on price: divide; on cost: multiply.

viva.q: What is a composite cost unit?
viva.model: A unit combining two measures of service, such as tonne-km or patient-day, to capture both volume and distance or time.
By multiplying the load carried on each leg by the distance of that leg and adding the products.

viva.q: Name two running charges in transport.
viva.model: Fuel and lubricants, along with tyres and usage-based depreciation.

viva.q: Why is occupancy important in hotel costing?
viva.model: Because costs are largely fixed, so cost per room-day depends on how many rooms are actually occupied.

viva.q: What is the cost unit for power generation?
viva.model: The kilowatt-hour of electricity generated or supplied.

cases.title: City Clinic
cases.case: City Clinic has 40 beds; average occupancy 90% over 365 days. Annual ward costs: fixed ₹78,84,000, variable ₹500 per patient-day. It wants 25% profit on cost.

mcqs.explain: 78,84,000 ÷ 13,140 = 600. In practice: rises if occupancy falls.
600 fixed + 500 variable = 1,100. In practice: separate food and medicines.
